topic: The Great Depression and New Deal

question.leadin: One theory suggests that this woman and Fred Noonan died in the Mariana Islands while in Japanese custody.
question.text: Name this female aviator who left New Guinea aboard her plane, the Electra, but never arrived at Howland Island, which has spawned many theories about her disappearance.
question.clue: One theory surrounding the whereabouts of this person and their companion, Fred Noonan, was that they were executed by Japanese soldiers on Saipan.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the political career of Franklin D. Roosevelt.
swap.text: In 1932, FDR defeated this man to become president. This president's administration oversaw the beginning of the Great Depression, for which he was widely unpopular.
swap.clue: Near the end of his term, he sent Douglas MacArthur to clear out the Bonus Army that was protesting for relief from the Great Depression.

question.leadin: Name some organizations established during the New Deal.
question.text: This largest New Deal agency was created by the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935 and provided jobs and income to the unemployed; it also operated large arts, media, and literacy projects.
question.clue: One branch of this organization was led by Hallie Flanagan, under whose leadership that branch undertook news reenactments called the "Living Newspaper," series, while another branch of this organization was responsible for producing the American Guide Series.

swap.text: This 31 st president was largely blamed for the Great Depression, and disgruntled citizens set up makeshift shantytowns sarcastically nicknamed after him.
swap.clue: He was appointed head of food distribution in West Germany after WWII due to his successful heading of the US Food Administration after WWI.

question.leadin: Answer some questions regarding tariffs in American history.
question.text: This tariff passed during Herbert Hoover's administration raised import duties to the second-highest level ever in American history. It is considered to be a main cause of the Great Depression.
question.clue: Franklin Delano Roosevelt signed the Reciprocal Trade Agreements Act of 1934 as a direct Democratic response to this Republican legislation.

swap.text: During this "dark day," the value of the Dow Jones fell some 12% as investors received margin calls and flooded the markets with cheap stocks. It would mark the end of the Roaring Twenties and usher in the Great Depression.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the founder of the Fifth Party System.
question.text: One of the major contributors to the New Deal was this member of the Brain Trust, who was the first director of the New York City Planning Commission and later governed Puerto Rico.
question.clue: In another role, this man was influenced by the ideas of Clarence Perry and Clarence Stein in trying to design three thousand self-sufficient communities while working with John Lansill, those communities being known as Greenbelt Towns.

swap.leadin: Besides FDR winning an election, a lot of cool things happened in 1932.
swap.text: Walter Waters led this group of angry World War I veterans demanding an early payment of their pension. MacArthur forcibly removed them.
swap.clue: Pelham Glassford twice reinstated Walter Waters as the leader of this group, which Gladwin Bland described as "an immense hobo jungle."

question.text: The author of Change, Hope, and the Bomb, David Eli Llienthal, served as its chairman for five years. For 15 points, name this New Deal agency which brought electric power to the rural Southeast.
question.clue: It originated with a scheme to end dependance on Chilean nitrate imports during the First World War, and one of its chief opponents was John Lewis, who feared for the economic health of the coal mines.

swap.text: As Vice President, Wallace argued with Jesse Jones, the extremely powerful head of this institution founded during the Hoover term to provide loans to banks and businesses.
swap.clue: This entity, at one point led by Jesse Jones, was created by the Hoover administration to hand out money to the states during the Great Depression.

question.leadin: Name the following events that occurred during the presidency of Herbert Hoover.
question.text: The laissez-faire approach of this man, Hoover's Secretary of the Treasury, worsened the Great Depression.
question.clue: Those proceedings occurred after this man financially backed Pittsburgh-based members of Cox's Army.

swap.text: The "Cross of Gold" speech is said to have inspired this politician's slogan "Every Man a King." This populist proposed pensions and free college education as part of his "Share Our Wealth" program.
swap.answerHtml: Huey Long [or Huey Pierce Long, Jr.; prompt on “the Kingfish”]
swap.clue: This ally of Father Charles Coughlin promoted socialist reforms in his Share the Wealth campaign which promised to make "every man a king."

question.leadin: A group of this many Black students in Rock Hill, South Carolina, pioneered the "Jail, No Bail" strategy after being arrested at a sit-in.
question.text: What number also appears in the most common name of a 1972 anti-discrimination provision in education authored primarily by Patsy Mink?
question.answerHtml: nine [accept Title IX; accept Friendship Nine or Rock Hill Nine]
question.clue: Countee Cullen wrote about a group of this many people that ends "Surely, I said, / Now will the poets sing. / But they have raised no cry. / I wonder why."

swap.leadin: Journalist Dainis Ivans ("dye-niss EE-vons") rose to popularity, and eventually became the first leader of Tautas Fronte, after successfully opposing a proposed structure of this type.
swap.text: Name these structures. The illicit trade of caviar in Russia increased when sturgeon populations decreased after the building of one of these structures on the Volga River.
swap.clue: Argentina briefly opposed the building of one of these structures, named Itaipu, between Paraguay and Brazil on the Paran´a River.

question.text: New York City's chief medical examiner, who had this surname, noted that the government "knows it is not stopping drinking" by poisoning alcohol. A senator with this surname drafted workers' rights legislation with Fiorello LaGuardia.

swap.text: The invasion of Manchuria caused the U.S. to issue this policy, saying that the U.S. would not recognize forcible territorial change. It is named for Hoover's Secretary of State, who became FDR's Secretary of War.
swap.clue: The United Nations enshrined this idea in the eleventh article of the Draft Declaration on Rights and Duties of States.

question.leadin: Justice Harlan Stone's majority opinion ruled that a federal prohibition on the interstate shipping of "filled milk" was not unconstitutional.
question.text: Name this 1938 Supreme Court case, which is more famous for its "footnote four."
question.answer: United States v. Carolene Products Co
question.clue: This Supreme Court case, whose Footnote Four introduced the basis for strict scrutiny by proposing a "narrower scope for operation of the presumption of constitutionality."

swap.text: This Mayor of New York City from 1926 to 1932 publicized his visit to Tom Mooney while Mooney was in jail. His marriage to the Ziegfield showgirl Betty Compton gained him the nickname "Gentleman."
swap.answerHtml: Jimmy Walker [or James John Walker; or James J. Walker]

question.leadin: Tom McCoy was a principal actor in this event, which in the span of a single day used the favorable results of a recount to reorganize the entire government of Rhode Island.
question.text: Identify this pivotal event of Rhode Island history which took place on January 1, 1935, and in which a possible case of voter fraud allowed Democrats to assume complete control of state politics.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a piece of legislation FTPE.
swap.text: This 1933 piece of legislation sought to raise and stabilize farm prices, store reserves, and control production.
swap.clue: This bill that was later augmented by the Thomas Amendment, which allowed the President to create silver money and reduce the gold backing of the dollar.
